text: Top leader calls for stronger Guangdong-Vietnam supply chain links and technology transfer

During a meeting with Guangdong Party Secretary Huang Kunming on November 17, General Secretary and President To Lam of Vietnam called for stronger production and supply chain linkages between Guangdong and Vietnam, stressing the need to tie investment more closely to technology transfer and workforce training while creating conditions for Vietnamese businesses to participate more deeply in regional value chains.

The meeting took place in Shenzhen, Guangdong Province (China), on the sidelines of the top Vietnamese leader's attendance at the APEC 2026 Economic Leaders' Week and his working visit to China, according to the Vietnam News Agency.

General Secretary and President Lam congratulated Guangdong on its development achievements, particularly its role as one of China's leading economic, industrial and high-tech hubs, and as a key driver of the development of the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area.
For his part, Mr. Huang affirmed that the Party organization, government and people of Guangdong highly value their friendship and practical cooperation with Vietnam.
He pledged to continue effectively implementing the important common perceptions reached by the top leaders of the two parties and countries.

Both sides spoke positively of cooperation outcomes since the Vietnamese top leader's visit to Guangdong in August 2024, highlighting robust growth in trade, a shift in investment toward high-tech and advanced manufacturing sectors, and promising new opportunities in infrastructure and science and technology cooperation.

General Secretary and President Lam proposed promoting connectivity between the Greater Bay Area and Vietnamese localities; strengthening production and supply chain integration; linking investment with technology transfer and human resource development; and enabling Vietnamese enterprises to play a greater role in global value chains.

He also called on Guangdong to increase imports of Vietnam's competitive products, enhance logistics connectivity, and foster direct cooperation among universities, research institutes, innovation centers and technology enterprises.
In addition, he suggested closer collaboration in sharing experiences related to the organization of APEC events.

The Vietnamese top leader further urged effective implementation of the Vietnam-China Tourism Cooperation Year, greater preservation and promotion of historical sites in Guangdong associated with President Ho Chi Minh and the revolutionary history of both countries, as well as expanded cooperation in education, culture, arts and sports.

Agreeing with General Secretary and President Lam's proposals, Mr. Huang pledged to advance practical cooperation across a wide range of areas, particularly in trade, investment, science and technology.

He said Guangdong is ready to share its development achievements, encourage major corporations and high-tech enterprises to invest in Vietnam, and expand imports of Vietnamese agricultural products and fruits.

Mr. Huang also reaffirmed Guangdong's commitment to preserving historical sites linked to President Ho Chi Minh and other veteran Vietnamese revolutionaries, while promoting tourism, education and people-to-people exchanges between Guangdong and Vietnamese localities.
